properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/25/2022 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Wilmot Twp, Bradford county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/25/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 949213
Permit API: 015-23529
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wilmot Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/25/2022
Comments: Chesapeake Appalachia (CHK) called in a release of produced fluid at 14:48 on 3/24/22. The release was found around 13:30 the same day. It was reported that at least 1 barrel of produced fluid was released from secondary containment. I arrived onsite on 3/25/22 and met with Aaron Stredny, CHK, and Creston. The fluid was released from and improperly sealed hatch on the temporary storage tank onsite. The fluid then leaked from secondary containment through a hole in the corner. A lease operator was onsite earlier in the morning and did not notice any issues. It is believed that the release occurred during the morning of 3/24/22 until its discovery around 13:30. When I arrived an area behind the tank was already excavated to a depth of 6-12 inches. I checked conductivity of puddles and soil with Creston. The soil and puddles to west were below 1000 microsiemens. Moving east from the excavated area toward the pad berm puddles and soil were elevated upto 7800 microsiemens in some areas. Additional soil and puddles were checked outside the pad along the fill slope and into the neighboring field. Results were below 500 microsiemens. The excavation will continue in the areas of elevated conductivity to the west and under the secondary containment. CHK is waiting for Mountain Energy to remove the temporary tank and containment in order to excavate the area. Before the tank is moved surrounding puddles will be removed. At least 3 tri-axle loads were excavated. It is requested that CHK perform remediation of the site according to the requirements of Act 2 and provide the requested information indicated in this inspection.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/20/2025 to KRIEBEL NATURAL GAS CO LLC in Manor Borough, Westmoreland county. 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.

Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8226206
Permit API: 129-28077
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Manor Borough
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/20/2025
Comments: On March 20, 2025, the DEP conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Kriebel Natural Gas Co's RWS Development 001 Well located in Manor Borough, Westmoreland County in response to an incident which is documented in IR 3941481 and 3941519 where violations were issued for a brine release. Accompanying on today's inspection was Kriebel representative's Ben Dickun and Ronald Seich.At the time of this inspection, Mr. Dickun and Mr. Seich stated that the production tank on site had been emptied prior to our arrival on site and that they were going to install booms in the ditch that runs adjacent to the well site and terminates at a nearby stream downslope. The DEP inquired whether any other remediation efforts were going to be conducted while the DEP was on site or after the inspection, and Mr. Dickun stated that they were awaiting instruction from the DEP. At the time of this inspection, the DEP verbally recommended Kriebel promptly remediate the brine release in accordance with Act 2 protocol. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed charred vegetation on a slope adjacent to the well site, no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it, and no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this wellhead. Other production equipment was observed on site and appeared to be charred, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near any of this production equipment. A production tank was observed on site with a large hole in its side, the tank had approximately 1-2 in of fluid pooled at the bottom of it, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this production tank.During IR 3941481 and 3941519, the DEP collected several soil conductivity readings around the well site to determine the extent of the release and concluded that the brine release was contained to a ditch that runs alongside the well site edge and terminates just before a stream. No elevated conductivity readings were collected in the stream, therefore at the time of that inspection, it did not appear that there were any impacts to the Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC).At the time of this inspection, the DEP took a background soil conductivity upslope and away from the incident area (0.0833 mS), and then soil conductivity readings were taken within the ditch: Right by the production equipment (1.225 mS and 1.105 mS), right by a inlet that appeared to be plugged with rocks and plastic (1.165 mS), right by an outlet that appeared to be dry at the time of this inspection (0.828 mS), and then in the ditch leading up to where it terminates just before the stream (1.132 mS, 1.236 mS, and 1.348 mS,). Readings taken directly upslope of the ditch on both sides were comparable to the background reading, while readings taken inside the ditch were elevated, subjugating that the release still appears to be contained to the ditch. To determine whether the stream had become impacted from the brine release, at the time of this inspection, a soil conductivity readings was taken on the stream bank directly downslope of where the ditch terminates (0.593 mS), then a soil (0.402 mS) and fluid (0.459 mS) conductivity reading was taken in the stream directly downslope of where the ditch terminates and lastly, a fluid reading was taken upslope (0.527 mS) and downslope (0.524 mS) of this area. Based on the DEP's observations and these conductivity readings, it appears that the WOC at the time of this inspection remain unscathed from the brine release. The DEP recommends immediate measures are properly implemented to commence remediation in response to the brine release that occurred onsite during the 3/19/2025 incident to prevent further migration of the onsite pollution and prevent pollution into WOC.Based on today's inspection, violations issued during IR 3941481 and 3941519 shall remain outstanding.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 91.33(A) - INCIDENTS CAUSING OR THREATENING POLLUTION - Failure to notify the Department of an accident or other activity or incident, a toxic substance or another substance which would endanger downstream users of the waters, result in pollution or create a danger of pollution of the waters of this Commonwealth, or would damage property.
Violation ID: 965088
Permit API: 053-27695
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/11/2022
Comments: This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the location.Upon arriving on the location, I observed two areas of recent earth disturbance to the west/northwest of the well. The first area is in the proximity of a pipeline riser where patches of oil soaked soil remain across the excavated area. A second area located northwest of the riser (beyond the edge of the location) contains oil soaked ground and crude oil floating atop standing water in depressed areas. A third area of oil soaked ground/leaf litter was also observed approximately 100 feet into the woods to the west of the well. There are no signs of recent excavation in this area, there is no apparent surface connection between this area and the prior two.These observations indicate a recent partial cleanup of a crude oil release from the riser. Additional cleanup measures will be required throughout the area near the riser and northwest of the riser in order for those areas to be considered sufficiently remediated. As part of remediating the third area, due diligence should be given to establish the source of the product and any potential subsurface connection to the riser.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/21/2021 to SWN PROD CO LLC in Stevens Twp, Bradford county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SWN PROD CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/21/2021
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 934591
Permit API: 015-22245
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Stevens Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/21/2021
Comments: On 10/21/2021, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident inspection at the Greenzweig (U Pad). This inspection is to evaluate the site after an engine oil spill was reported to the department on 10/20/2021. When I arrived on site I met two SWN personnel, Mike Deming and Seth Tratthen. Also on site were two men from Resource Environmental Management Inc. I have contact info for John Salinkas. Description of event: A compressor station is in the process of being removed from the site. A crew from a third party company, Pilot Thomas, was removing fluids from the equipment prior to the equipment being loaded on trucks. Unused engine oil was being transferred from a 500-gallon tank to a 300-gallon tote that was already on a truck. The tote did not have a cap on the two inch drain valve and the tote was strapped down on the truck with the drain valve not immediately accessible by the crew. As the crew was pumping into the tote, they suspected something was wrong with the pumping process. They checked the progress and found the drain valve partially open and leaking fluids onto the ground. They stopped pumping and had to unstrap the tote before manhandling it to a position where they could reach and close the valve. It is estimated that 120 gallons of HDAX 5200 Low Ash Gas Engine OIl was released onto the unprotected ground. This was next to edge of the pad. A perimeter berm kept the fluid from flowing off property and down the fill slope. Response: A truck on site that could pick up fluids was used to collect 90 gallons of free liquid. A skid-steer was brought to location and excavated a 40' long x10' wide x2.5' (maximum measurements) trench. The excavated material was loaded into two 30yd rolloff dumpsters. While I was still on site, both dumpsters were loaded onto trucks and hauled away to an industrial landfill. I was shown the excavated area where the spill had impacted. I did not witness any signs of free liquid or additional contamination. I was told that the cleanup crew tested the excavation area to determine if clear of contamination before ending excavation. No E&S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. The site appears stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. There are a total of 3 wells staged for production. All wells are tagged with API/well permit numbers. The well cellars are filled with gravel. All GPUs and production tanks were stationed in secondary containment. This spill constitutes violations of these three regulations 78a 56(a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b) The department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance with 78a 66(c).

Violation ID: 8275338

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/14/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted to evaluate the status of violations issued on 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 associated with the construction of the well site for this proposed conventional well and the access road leading to it. Since the 4/17/2026 inspection, Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) submitted multiple versions of an updated E and S plan that included additional BMPs and methods to stabilize all disturbed areas. At the time of this inspection, the latest version of the updated E and S plan has not yet met the expectations of the Department's Technical Services staff, as was indicated in a 5/11/2026 email to William Cenk.Throughout this inspection, we observed that a majority of the practices prescribed in the latest version of the updated E and S plan have been implemented. Inlet/outlet rock protection was placed at the installed culverts, rock filters placed in the roadside ditch in the vicinity of the well site for proposed Well # 3, and a combination of erosion blankets and mulch was applied to temporarily stabilize most of the disturbed areas. TMP indicated that seed was applied prior to mulching/placement of the erosion blanket. Erosion blanket was missing upslope of Culvert 1 and there was no evidence of hydro-seeding. The placement of grubbing material along the southern side of the access road that has displaced stream flow continues to result in accelerated erosion and washout along the southern edge of the road and perimeter of the well site for proposed Well # 4.The Department suggests the removal of the stockpile material from approximately the outlet location of Culvert 3 westerly to the newly established point of concentrated flow. Comments: On 08/25/2025, a complaint inspection was conducted at the plugged Blum 1 Well Site following receipt of a complaint (CTS 391464). The well was plugged on 12/12/2019. I was accompanied by Water Quality Specialist Jena Bonasorte (PA DEP).The following was observed:The well appeared to be plugged. A monument with the well's permit number was on location. The permit number on the monument was incorrect and should read 37-125-22119-00. It appears that several pieces of casing remain at the plugging location (Photos 1-3).I observed several spots of oil/grease on the ground around the plugged well and what appears to be a demolished compressor station or dehydration system (Photos 4-9).The well site around the plugged well was not completely restored to original contour and vegetated. The adjacent compressor station was demolished, however equipment was present and piping remained. Pipes and electrical equipment were sticking out of the ground (Photos 2, 10-17).The access road was restored but appears to still be used (Photos 18, 19).The area where production tanks were previously, as seen on aerial imagery, displayed bare dirt (Photos 20-22). The tanks were not noted. Conductivity readings were obtained and no elevated readings were noted.The Department has not received a Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) from the operator following plugging. I recommend that the WSRR is submitted. Due to the operator failing to submit a WSRR within 60 days after restoration of the well site, failure to restore the site to original conditions, and failure to remove equipment/facilities, violations of 78.65(3), OGA3216(A), and OGA3216(D) are being issued.

Comments: On 11/18/2024, I conducted an inspection of the Hunters Cave 3 OG Well in Center Township, Greene County in response to a diesel spill reported to the Departments Emergency Hotline on 11/18/2024 (CTS #385283). The spill, reported by EQT, stated that approximately 25 gallons of diesel fuel had spilled on the Hunters Cave 3 OG Well Pad while a contractor was changing out a fuel filter. The report stated that no impacts to Waters of the Commonwealth occurred, and SPSI were on site conducting spill remediation.While on site, I spoke to a contractor with SPSI who stated that SPSI estimated the diesel fuel spill was approximately 50 gallons. SPSI utilized a PID meter to obtain VOC measurements of the impacted area. At the time of inspection, SPSI was actively excavating impacted aggregate and indicated that some areas within the delineated spill remained above 5 ppm. Further excavation would occur to achieve VOC readings below 5 ppm. SPSI planned to backfill the excavation once readings were below 5 ppm. While on site, I observed the following:-The Hunters Cave 3 OG Well Act 9 sign was located at the site entrance. A mailbox containing Emergency Response Plans (ERP), site plans, and a well permit was located at the site entrance (Photos 1-2).-The site entrance and access road appeared to be in generally good condition (Photo 3).-The diesel spill was located on the left side of the pad, outside of the perimeter of the sound barriers installed along the pad. The excavated area was approximately 20 ft x 20 ft, with a depth of 2-4 inches. SPSI was actively excavating impacted material at the time of inspection, and a PID meter was used to obtain VOC readings within the excavation (Photos 4-6).-A rolloff box was staged across from the spill, containing impacted aggregate that was excavated by SPSI. I observed a strong diesel fuel smell being emitted from the impacted aggregate (Photos 7-8).-Two pad stormwater drains, located approximately 150 feet below the spill, did not appear to contain diesel fuel. I observed inlet protection within both stormwater drains (Photos 9-10).-The well pad slopes on either side of the diesel fuel spill appeared to be in good condition, and I observed no indication that the diesel fuel spill exited the gravel pad (Photos 11-12).-A drilling rig was staged on site at the time of inspection (Photos 13-14).Due to the diesel fuel spill release exceeding 42 gallons (1 barrel), violations of 78.54, 91.34(A), and SWMA 301 are being issued to the Hunters Cave 3 OG Well.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/11/2022 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/11/2022
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 961505
Permit API: 081-21878
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/11/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted as a follow-up after on 6/24/2022, the operator reported a release of 140 barrels of produced fluid to the secondary containment, some of which then overflowed the secondary containment and flowed onto the pad surface. I first inspected Pad B. I met with company man Walt Arnold upon arriving on location. I saw a piece of discarded secondary containment that was sitting on the rig mats for the sandboxes near the pad entrance. Some fluid was dripping off of the containment and onto the rig mats. I asked the company man if there was secondary containment beneath the rig mats and he said no. I recommended to him that the discarded containment be placed on secondary containment until it could be thrown away. He said that he would have someone put it on secondary containment right away. Before I left the pad, the discarded containment was on its own secondary containment. Fluid with a electrical conductivity (EC) of >19.99 mS/cm as measured by the Oakton conductivity meter is present on the secondary containment for the blender. The Department recommends vacuuming out the containment. Fluid with an EC of between 1.6 to 2.3 mS/cm was observed on the pad surface near the northeast corner of the pad where some secondary containment was removed from the pad surface. The Department recommends scraping up the fluid in this area of the pad. Along the east side of the pad, at the southeast corner of the secondary containment for the produced water tanks, I observed staining and dampness on the pad surface. I also observed the dampness beneath the secondary containment berm as well. The fluid beneath the berm had an EC of >19.99 mS/cm as measured by the Oakton conductivity meter. The fluid present inside the containment also had an EC of >19.99 mS/cm. I also got the same reading when I pressed the meter probes into the mud on the pad surface. The visibly impacted area adjacent to the secondary containment was approximately 5 square feet in total. The surface area impacted beneath the secondary containment is unknown. When the berm of the secondary containment was lifted by EQT personnel, the pad surface beneath the containment appeared damp. I took a soil sample from the pad surface adjacent to the containment berm and slightly beneath the berm. There was not enough fluid on the pad surface to take a water sample. The sample is number 0718-196 which will be sent to the state laboratory to be analyzed for SAC 530 + Li and Br. Violations pending sample results.I also met with Rick Hall of EQT during this inspection and I showed him the area where I found the dampness, staining, and fluid at the corner of the produced water secondary containment. Violations remain outstanding for the release on 6/24/2022.

Code § 102.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/18/2023
Violation Code: 78a53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL AND STORMWATER MANAGEMENT - Person proposing or conducting earth disturbance activities associated with oil and gas operations failed to comply with 25 Pa. Code § 102.
Violation ID: 8162905
Permit API: 125-23693
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Mount Pleasant Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/18/2023
Comments: On 10/18/2023, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Cowden Unit 3H well site for violations cited on 3/24/2023 (SAIR 3528508, Enforcement ID: 415452, CID #370345). I was accompanied by PADEP Tech Services representatives Brian Bailey, Jeff Reidenbaugh and Samantha Kantorczky. The following was observed:Act 9 site ID sign installedThe well site entrance appeared to be maintained.Access Road Culvert #1 appeared open and functioningAccess road Culvert #2 inlet remains partially blocked with stone. The culvert remains constructed without a channel to covey stormwater runoff toward the culvert. Previously the Department requested clarification regarding the area. The Operators 5/19/2023 violation response suggests that the culvert may convey subsurface water. Access Road Culvert #3 inlet remains partially blocked with stone. DEP Technical services staff have looked over the site and have reviewed the file. In discussion with the complainant/ property owner the complainant stated that they are an 18 year resident of the home. According to the complainant , flooding wasnt as issue until the well pad was constructed. The well site was permitted in 2009, and appears to have been constructed toward the end of the 2009. Photos shown by the complainant show significant rainfall events occurring within the photos. However, significant flows were noted at areas where no earth disturbance occurred upgradient. As significant flows were noted elsewhere, no determination can be made utilizing the photos as to any impacts that are occurring from the well pad. The complainants house was noted to have fill elevated around the structure itself. This fill diverts any surface flows away from the house. The complainants stated that he gets feet of water within the residence, and also acknowledges he likely does not have any subsurface drains to drain subsurface flows away from the basement. A review of the plans and this site visit did not provide any information indicating any stormwater control measures were constructed with the construction of the well pad. The Department is requesting Range Resources provide calculations and supporting documents to show compliance with Chapter 102.8 within the next 30-days the Cowden Well site and associated access road. Determination:Violations remain outstanding

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 4/15/2022
Comments: On April 15th, 2022, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill incident reported to the Department for the Gospel Church Unit 10H Well Site in Plum Borough, Allegheny County. The Department reached out to Marc Jacobs of Penneco for additional information on the spill. Per Mr. Jacobs, the well tender discovered the spill on 4/15/2022. The spill occurred at a broken valve on one of the production tanks due to freeze/thaw. They estimate approximately 1 barrel of crude oil has been released and contained within the earthen dike. Cleanup crews have been called to the site. At this time, released oil is being absorbed with pads and peat soil until remediation efforts can continue on Monday. On Monday, 3rd party consultant (Woodard Curran) will be onsite to evaluate release. The affected production tanks will be removed and release area will be remediated. At time of inspection, several Penneco representatives were onsite finishing preliminary clean up efforts. Per Penneco representative, the release was discovered around 10am on 4/15/2022 by the well tender. The spill was estimated to occur sometime between 4/12/2022 (the last visit to the well site) and 4/15/2022. Penneco rep estimated release to be about 1 barrel at the production tank. A vacuum truck was onsite to remove surface crude oil from the release site. Rep stated that on 4/18/2022, two of the three tanks are to be removed and release area to be excavated. Release site was isolated within the dike around the production tanks. Absorbent pads and peat laid within the release area. The broken valve and pipe laid within the dike. There also appeared to be a release at the well head. Per Penneco Rep, there was a release of approximately 5 gallons from around the pump jack. Follow up inspection to be conducted upon completion of remediation efforts. The Department recommends Operator remediate impacted area IAW spill policy for releases greater than 42 gallons. The Department requests the following: disposal records/ manifests for removal of all impacted materials once available, quantity released at the production tank valve and at the well head, how quantity was determined, method of remediation, timeline of when the remediation will be completed, when the release around the wellhead occurred, why the release around the well head occurred and what was released at the well head. Based on today's observations, violations are being issued.

The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has been confirmed. No additional violations noted today. I departed the site at 1010 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/17/2025 to EQT PROD CO in Morris Township, Greene county. 78a64a(b) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – All regulated substances, including solid wastes and other regulated substances in equipment or vehicles, failed to be managed within secondary containment on the well site.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT PROD CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/17/2025
Violation Code: 78a64a(b) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – All regulated substances, including solid wastes and other regulated substances in equipment or vehicles, failed to be managed within secondary containment on the well site.
Violation ID: 8249212
Permit API: 059-27655
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Morris Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/17/2025
Comments: On 09/17/2025, an incident inspection was conducted at the Harden Farms Well Site following receipt of an incident report that was submitted to the Department on 09/17/2025 at 12:17 (CTS 392314).It was reported that 10 gallons of biocide material was spilled on site at 12:00, 09/17/2025. No waterways were affected. It was also reported that a clean up crew (SPSI) was on site.I called the EQT representative who reported the spill, Lance Witters, for information. I noted that SPSI arrived after I did, and I requested the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) to be sent to me. It was described to me that the material spilled was a Multi-Chem biocide. The cause of the release was that a hose back pressured, biocide flowed back to the tank, and the tank overflowed. It was estimated that 10 gallons spilled.SPSI had not began remediation and was not on the pad when I arrived. No personal were on the pad upon my arrival.The following was observed:The contaminated area was adjacent to the gas production units (GPUs). It was unknown if any production fluid was present in addition to the biocide spilled; no elevated conductivity was observed. No remediation had begun and SPSI was not on the pad when I arrived on the pad. SPSI arrived to the site after the Department (Photo 1). An extremely strong odor was experienced on site in the vicinity of the contaminated area.SPSI then arrived on the pad and had not begun remediation while I was on site. The impacted area was located between the well heads and the GPUs. The impacted area appeared wet with small sections of pooled fluid (Photos 2-5).I asked SPSI if they had the SDS, and they did not. The SDS was not located on site with the site documents in the mailboxes. I was able to locate a Control and Disposal Plan and the Site Specific Safety and Environmental Plan and Policy. I was not able to locate any information related to the Multi-Chem biocide (Photos 6-9). I also did not find a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan (PPC) on site. The SDSs are required to be on site. The PPC Plan is also required to be on site during drilling or completion activities, however the well operator shall prepare and develop a site specific PPC plan prior to storing, using, or generating regulated substances to, on or from a well site.The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance (Photo 10).The Department requests a description of the activities that were being carried out that resulted in a spill.Due to the SDS not present on site, a PPC Plan not on site, failure to control regulated fluids with a release to the ground, and failure to use secondary containment, violations of 78a.54, 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(i)5iD, SWMA 301, 91.34(a), and 78a64a(b) are being issued.
